# (BL-378) pole register, in the standing-red register's shape (BL-1428). A
# row names an OPEN ticket that owns bringing its file back under budget: a
# file over budget WITH a row here is reported, not refused; a file over
# budget WITHOUT a row refuses as new-pole; a row whose file now measures
# under 80% of the budget refuses as stale (the row leaves in the same land
# that cut the pole); a row naming a closed or absent ticket refuses as
# unowned. Measured 2026-09-16 (specifier npm test run for BL-791 slice C,
# 20 cores, 9 forks, 1-minute load 10.8; extension/.vitest-report.json) -
# never a rounded-down value. Slice D tickets take rows over as they are
# minted; a row drains automatically in the same land that cuts its pole -
# the land step retires every row this register lists whose owner is the
# landing ticket (BL-1631: REGISTER_ROW_RETIRED), EXCEPT an accepted-pole
# row (disposition column below, BL-1629), which the land step never
# retires regardless of owner.
# file
# disposition is optional: a row with no 5th column (or 'owned' spelled
# out) is owned, exactly as before BL-1629. 'accepted' names a pole that
# will not be cut - ticket holds the rationale ticket (may be closed),
# note carries "re-measure: YYYY-MM-DD".
